text:
alex: Heads-up — spotted a perf regression on sm91 when serving INT4 at seqlen=512. Kernel selector is choosing the FP8-path for some shards, latency up ~2x vs baseline. I have a short profile attached.
perf-bot: Quick summary: sm91 / int4 / seqlen=512 / batch=8 -> mean latency 118ms (was 58ms). Hotspots: kernel_dispatch.cpp:line 224, kv_cache_manager.cpp:evict_sync
li: Uploading flamegraph + tiny perf sample. Looks like a pathflip in select_kernel() where cost_estimator prefers fp8 for conv-like matmuls at this seqlen.
maria: Is this only at batch=8? any effect at batch=4 or 16?
li: batch=4: 62ms (close to baseline). batch=16: 220ms (worse). So it's seqlen+batch interaction — middle batches force a different working set and kernel choice.
jon: Could be cache-line footprint + workspace allocation pushing us over a heuristic threshold. Also seeing more KV eviction calls during generation warmup.
alex: Small log snippet:
```
[2026-02-11T14:03:12Z] select_kernel: arch=sm91 quant=INT4 seqlen=512 batch=8 -> pick=fp8_matmul_v2(cost=213ms)
[2026-02-11T14:03:12Z] kv_cache_manager: evict_sync triggered (size_delta=46MB)
[2026-02-11T14:03:12Z] launch_kernel: fp8_matmul_v2 workspace_alloc=128MB
```
maria: Two hypotheses: 1) cost_estimator weights for memory vs latency are skewed for sm91; 2) KV warmup/eviction is increasing workspace pressure so selector chooses smaller-FLOP but FP8 path that's actually slower due to conversion overhead.
sam: Can we autotune a per-arch param like seqlen_split_point or prefer_int4_threshold? If we bump the seqlen_split_point up for sm91 maybe keep INT4 kernels for 512.
jon: I prototyped a toggle: kernel_hint{arch:sm91}.seqlen_bias = -64 — made selector prefer the int4 path up to 576. Quick local numbers (tokens/sec):
- before (master): 450 t/s
- with seqlen_bias=-64: 820 t/s
- with seqlen_bias=-128: 840 t/s (no regression on other seqlens in my small tests)
li: Also tested kv_warmup_chunks: default=1 -> warmup triggers eviction mid-stream. Setting kv_warmup_chunks=3 spreads warmup and avoids sudden alloc spikes. Combined with seqlen_bias=-64 gives stable 780-860 t/s across batch sizes.
alex: Nice. Any regression on sm95/sm92 with that bias?
jon: I ran sm92 quick: negligible change. sm95: small +3% improvement in some cases. So bias looks safe across these sampled archs.
maria: We should add an autotune job that sweeps seqlen_bias per-arch and kv_warmup_chunks per-workload. Can we hook into the existing perf CI? @ci-bot
ci-bot: perf job scheduled: ci/perf/arch-tune/194120 — will run sm91, sm92, sm95 across seqlens [128,256,512,1024] and batches [4,8,16]. Results link: https://ci.redwood/incoming/194120
li: FYI there's a microbench that reproduces the flip: scripts/bench/kernel_selector_flip.sh (use --arch sm91 --quant int4 --seqlen 512 --batch 8)
sam: Proposal: land a guarded feature flag (runtime flag: prefer_int4_until=seqlen) + experiment config so we can ramp on Dedicated clusters. Then follow with an autotune sweep to populate defaults per-arch.
alex: Agreed. Plan: (1) PR with seqlen_bias param + KV warmup tuning (draft by @jon), (2) CI perf sweep, (3) canary on dedicated, (4) rollout if green.
jon: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287 (draft) — includes config, unit tests, and perf hook for CI.
li: Attaching the flamegraph id: fg_194120_001 (uploaded to perf-artifacts). Main takeaway: FP8 path spends extra time in dtype conversion kernels and workspace allocs when eviction spikes.
maria: One more ask — add a small telemetry metric: kernel_path_choice{arch,quant,seqlen,batch} to see how often selector flips in prod.
alex: Good call. Add that to PR. Also add a guard so default remains conservative until CI sweep passes.
sam: I'll own the canary rollout once PR is merged. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
perf-bot: CI perf job completed (partial): sm91/int4/seqlen=512/batch=8 -> master: 58ms, pr-4287: 31ms, delta -46.6% — full results pending.
ci-bot: full results: https://ci.redwood/incoming/194120/results.json
alex: Closing loop tomorrow after full artifacts. If anyone finds further edge cases post-merge ping here.
